item.title: Using a public washroom
item.description: Find a public washroom, read common signs, and learn words for the things you use there.

children.definition: A room in a public place where you can use the toilet and wash your hands.
children.example: Excuse me, where is the washroom in this shopping centre?

children.definition: A solid or liquid that you use with water to wash your hands.
children.example: There's no soap in the washroom by the station exit.

children.definition: Something you use to start and stop the flow of water from a pipe, for example at a sink.
children.example: This tap turns on when you put your hands under it.

children.definition: A large bowl with a hole for water to go down. You can wash your hands in it.
children.example: You can use the sink by the door while I finish washing my hands.
collocations: wash your hands at the sink

children.definition: A machine that blows air to take water off your hands.
children.example: Put your hands under the hand dryer by the exit.

children.definition: A piece of thick paper you can use to dry your hands.
children.example: The hand dryer isn't working, so take a paper towel from the box by the sink.

children.definition: Soft paper you use to clean yourself after using the toilet.
children.example: There isn't any toilet paper in the first cubicle.

children.definition: A piece of glass you can look in to see your face.
children.example: I checked my hair in the washroom mirror before the interview.

children.definition: A container for things you want to throw away.
children.example: Please put used paper towels in the bin by the door.

children.definition: To close a door with a lock so it stays shut until someone unlocks it.
children.example: You can turn this to lock the cubicle door from the inside.
collocations: lock the door from the inside

children.definition: To make water go through the toilet to clean it after use.
children.example: Press the round button to flush the toilet.
The small washroom is occupied, so I'll wait by the door.

children.definition: Not working and so you cannot use it.
children.example: The sign says the toilet is out of order, so let's use the one upstairs.
collocations: the toilet is out of order
the hand dryer is out of order

children.definition: A small space with a door and a toilet inside a public washroom.
children.example: The cubicle next to the sinks has a broken lock.
